card.name: Pavane
card.tagline: Renaissance Europe — the slow processional dance once used at funerals. Dancers wore swords because nobody could move fast enough to fight.
card.profile: Renaissance Europe, 1500s — the slow processional dance once used at funerals in Spain and Italy. Dancers wore swords because nobody could move quickly enough to fight. Maurice Ravel's 1899 "Pavane pour une infante défunte" preserved its melody for the modern world.
card.insight: Italian dancing master Fabritio Caroso codified the pavane in his 1581 manual 'Il Ballarino'; the dance's stately tempo of 60-70 beats per minute matched the resting heartbeat of European nobility — making it the slowest formal dance in 16th-century court culture.
